plan.topic: Retatrutide and the kidneys: TRANSCEND-CKD, a 24-week trial in adults with obesity and chronic kidney disease (HCPLive, Oct 22, 2026)
plan.angle: Hook: 'Can retatrutide protect the kidneys?' Answer: 'In a 24-week trial presented at ASN Kidney Week (Oct 2026, reported by HCPLive on 22 Oct 2026), people with a baseline urine albumin of 30 or more saw it fall about 54% on retatrutide versus 9% on placebo. That's a placebo-adjusted difference of 49.2%.' Define UACR as 'urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, an early sign of kidney strain'. Population: 'adults with BMI 27 or higher and chronic kidney disease, with or without type 2 diabetes; 75 on retatrutide, 71 on placebo'. Then: 'No significant difference in measured kidney filtration. This is an early marker, not proof it prevents kidney failure. A large Phase 3 trial, TRIUMPH-Outcomes, is testing heart and kidney outcomes, with results expected around 2029 per ClinicalTrials.gov.' Status: 'Investigational, not approved anywhere as of 25 Oct 2026.' GI line: 'In earlier retatrutide trials, nausea and diarrhoea were common.' Never mention online products; for approved options or a trial, ask a prescriber; then 'not personal advice', the prescriber line, and 'follow for more'. On screen: 'early marker · 24 weeks · baseline UACR ≥30 subgroup · not kidney-failure outcomes · investigational'. 170 words or fewer.
plan.working_title: Can Retatrutide Protect the Kidneys? What 24 Weeks Showed #shorts
plan.why: Fresh Phase 2 data on our highest-peaking Shorts name (253, 196, 120) that only clinician press has covered so far. It adds a fact we haven't published: retatrutide and kidney markers. | fact-check: Verified via HCPLive (TRANSCEND-CKD, presented at ASN Kidney Week, Oct 21–25, 2026, Denver) and NCT05936151. What's wrong in the plan: (a) The population is adults with BMI 27 or higher and established CKD, with or without type 2 diabetes, and cystatin C eGFR 25–75. That is not just 'obesity'. (b) Group sizes are 75 on retatrutide (escalated to 12 mg) and 71 on placebo. (c) In HCPLive, the −49.2% is the placebo-adjusted difference among people with baseline UACR ≥30 mg/g (−53.7% versus −8.8%). It is not a separate overall figure, so present one number, not two. (d) For GFR, say 'no significant difference between groups in measured GFR', not 'didn't change'. (e) TRIUMPH-Outcomes isn't in HCPLive. Credit it to ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06383390 instead: Phase 3, about 10,000 adults with BMI 27 or higher and heart/blood-vessel disease and/or CKD, cardiovascular and kidney outcomes, estimated primary completion Feb 2029. (f) HCPLive doesn't report nausea or diarrhoea for this trial, so the GI line must be credited to retatrutide's earlier trials or dropped. (g) This is a conference presentation, not a peer-reviewed paper; say 'presented at'.

package.title: Retatrutide and Kidneys: What a New CKD Trial Found #shorts
package.description:
Retatrutide and kidneys: in a 24-week trial, adults with BMI 27 or higher and chronic kidney disease took retatrutide or placebo. In the roughly 3 in 10 who started with UACR of 30 mg/g or higher, it fell 53.7% vs 8.8% on placebo, but measured kidney filtration didn't significantly differ. Nausea and diarrhoea were common in earlier trials; pulse rose 9 bpm here. Investigational, not approved anywhere as of October 25, 2026; Lilly said July 23, 2026 it plans to file with the FDA in Q1 2027.

social.instagram_caption:
Kidney labs got you a little worried? Here's what a new retatrutide trial actually found.

• Over 24 weeks, adults with BMI 27 or higher and chronic kidney disease (with or without type 2 diabetes) took retatrutide, built up to 12 mg weekly, or placebo.
• In the roughly 3 in 10 who started with UACR (a urine marker of kidney strain) of 30 mg/g or higher, it fell 53.7% on retatrutide vs 8.8% on placebo — a 49.2% placebo-adjusted difference at 24 weeks.
• The catch: the trial's main goal, measured kidney filtration, didn't significantly differ between groups. An early marker improving isn't proof it prevents kidney failure.
• Common side effects in earlier retatrutide trials include nausea and diarrhoea; pulse rose 9 bpm on retatrutide here.
• Status: investigational, not approved anywhere as of October 25, 2026. Lilly said on July 23, 2026 it plans to file with the FDA in Q1 2027.

Save this for the next time kidney health or GLP-1 research comes up.

Phase 3 TRIUMPH-Outcomes is testing heart and kidney outcomes in about 10,000 adults aged 45 or older with BMI 27 or higher and heart or blood-vessel disease, kidney disease, or both (estimated primary completion February 2029, per ClinicalTrials.gov). script.hook_pattern: Opens on a question that names the drug ("Can retatrutide protect your kidneys?"), followed by a recognition beat ("Kidney labs worrying you? Fair."). Setup: TRANSCEND-CKD, presented at Kidney Week 2026, in adults with BMI 27 or higher and chronic kidney disease, 75 on retatrutide versus 71 on placebo, with UACR defined in plain English. Payoff: the UACR drop in the roughly 3-in-10 subgroup whose UACR started at 30 mg/g or higher, with both groups' figures beside the placebo-adjusted difference. Re-hook with "the catch": the main goal, measured kidney filtration, didn't significantly differ between groups. Then the Phase 3 outcomes trial still to come (credited to ClinicalTrials.gov, with its estimated date), side effects including this trial's pulse rise, the dated status and Lilly's dated filing plan, and the prescriber line. Ends on a soft "follow for more" because today's long-form is about petrelintide, so there's no funnel link.

factcheck.summary: I checked every factual claim against its source, and they all hold up. HCPLive (22 Oct 2026) confirms these TRANSCEND-CKD details: Phase 2b, presented at ASN Kidney Week 2026, adults with BMI 27 or higher and CKD with or without type 2 diabetes, 75 on retatrutide versus 71 on placebo, the dose built up from 2 mg to 12 mg over 16 weeks and kept at 12 mg to week 24, and about 30% starting with UACR of 30 mg/g or higher. In that subgroup UACR fell 53.7% versus 8.8%, a difference of −49.2% (95% CI −70.6% to −12.3%). The main goal, measured kidney filtration (mGFR), showed no significant difference (−1.4, 95% CI −9.2 to 6.3). Pulse rose 9.0 bpm (95% CI 5.7–12.3). The ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT05936151 matches the title, Phase 2b, 146 people enrolled and the week-24 mGFR main goal. The ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT06383390 (TRIUMPH-Outcomes) matches: about 10,000 people (estimated), aged 45 or older, BMI 27 or higher, atherosclerotic heart or blood-vessel disease and/or CKD, heart and kidney outcomes as main goals, and main results due February 2029 (estimated; record updated 8 Oct 2026). HCPLive (23 Jul 2026) confirms Lilly plans to file with the FDA in Q1 2027. The NDT design paper's details check out. The NEJM and Lancet Phase 2 papers support "nausea and diarrhoea common". No approval anywhere could be found as of 25 Oct 2026. The framing is honest: the uncertainty is stated clearly (early marker, main goal missed, no kidney-failure outcomes), the subgroup is scoped, both groups' figures sit beside the difference, the drug is labelled investigational and the prescriber line is there. The hook question gets an honest answer. Two wording points should be tightened, and the script is over the 170-word guide for Shorts.

issues.claim: in this trial, pulse rose nine beats per minute on retatrutide at twenty-four weeks
issues.problem: HCPLive gives the +9.0 bpm with a confidence interval, which suggests it is a between-group (placebo-adjusted) figure. Saying it 'rose nine on retatrutide' may misstate what the number measures.
issues.fix: Narration: "and in this trial, pulse was about nine beats per minute higher on retatrutide than on placebo at twenty-four weeks." List item: "TRANSCEND-CKD: pulse about +9 bpm vs placebo, 24 weeks"

issues.claim: with heart or blood-vessel disease, kidney disease, or both
issues.problem: The ClinicalTrials.gov entry criterion is established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral artery disease). 'Heart or blood-vessel disease' is broader, though acceptable as plain English.
issues.fix: Narration: "with artery disease of the heart, brain or legs, kidney disease, or both." Stat label: "Adults 45+, BMI ≥27, atherosclerotic heart/vessel disease and/or kidney disease"

issues.problem: The narration is about 260 words, well over the 170-word Shorts guide. It is still under the 178 s hard limit (about 100–110 s).

audio.soundNotes: Trimmed redundant stacked SFX in several dense clusters (intro, label reveals, the −49.2% stat, "the catch" transition, +9.0 bpm reveal) down to 2–3 effects each per the 3–4/sec rule, and pulled down a handful of cues that were sitting too close to the voice (−12.7 to −13.6 dB) during speech to the −14/−15 dB felt zone. Left pause/transition cues (e.g. around 2.3s, 30s, 51.5–51.8s, 61.8s) at their louder −7 to −11 dB levels since those land in silence. Music is already in the right window (−13.5 dB under voice) so only a small safety trim (0.9×) given the channel's recurring masking holds; kept it present under speech and let it breathe a bit in the pause before "the catch" and after the big UACR reveal. Added a few bespoke beats (kidney filtration, heartbeat for the heart-rate stat, a tension sting for "the catch") to carry emotion the stock kit can't, all kept subtle and under the voice.
